title: A website for understanding Starter
question: The systems atlas gives the overview, essay, and guide one coherent visual language. Choose it, take the notebook alternate, or steer the direction.

options.label: Systems atlas
options.thesis: A readable atlas of how a question becomes a project, with diagrams you can explore.
options.viewport: Oversized left-aligned title above a wide live map: a brief, project knowledge, work, and evidence.
options.risk: Diagrams must explain real relationships, never become decorative complexity.

regions.label: A place for the work to grow.

raised.raise: Make state transitions legible without relying on color.
Own the first viewport with one decisive composition.
Give the long essay a sustained reading rhythm.
Show what each step adds rather than merely naming it.
Keep a clear still state for every animation.

options.label: Computational notebook
options.thesis: An original essay with working figures embedded directly into the argument.
options.viewport: Essay title, short abstract, and an executable project example before the first chapter.
options.risk: A familiar developer-docs arrangement; the overview may feel secondary.

options.label: Depot destination roll
options.thesis: A project stage moves into a fixed window.
options.viewport: A project stage moves into a fixed window.
options.risk: Its dense one-size legends hinder a long essay.
options.case: Declined on reader fit and explanatory clarity.
options.kept: Make state transitions legible without relying on color.

options.label: Film cutting bench
options.thesis: A verification sequence scrubs through frames.
options.viewport: A verification sequence scrubs through frames.
options.risk: Editing-film notation adds a metaphor to learn.
options.case: Declined on reader fit and explanatory clarity.

options.label: Layered street flyer
options.thesis: Projects assemble from overlapping source pieces.

options.kept: Own the first viewport with one decisive composition.

options.label: Copy-shop essay
